spec.title: Responses per second the client got (k6)
spec.description: k6 counters b8_resp_202 / b8_resp_503 / b8_resp_other (other = status 0, the client gave up after 10 s or the connection was refused/reset). Added by B8 in script.js: they exist in Prometheus only after a k6 run. Offered rate is flat (2000 req/s); 202 should fall to 0 (or near) in the fault and come back. Surprising: 202 never comes back (a pause_blackhole run may do that), or 'other' dominates instead of 503 (the client waits instead of being told).

spec.title: Events lost by a producer without retries (% not accepted)
spec.description: 100 x (503 + other) / all responses, per interval. Every request that is not a 202 is an event a producer that does not retry has lost. Added by B8 (k6 counters). Zero before the fault, high during it, and back to 0 after recovery. Surprising: not back to 0 long after the fault ended (the recovery lag).

spec.title: Client latency p50 / p99 (k6)
spec.description: k6_http_req_duration_seconds, native histogram, p50 and p99. A 503 from a refused connection is fast; a black hole shows latencies near the pool timeout (2 s) or the k6 request timeout (10 s). The p99 is clamped by the 10 s request timeout. Native histograms in a window with no requests give no point.

spec.title: Responses per second the server counted, by status
spec.description: http_requests_total of the server by status (/metrics excluded). It differs from the k6 panel when the client gave up before the server answered (those show up here only if the server answers later). Surprising: a lot more 202 here than in k6 after a pause = answers that arrived too late.

spec.title: Is Postgres up? (postgres-exporter pg_up)
spec.description: pg_up of the postgres-exporter job: 1 = the exporter could query Postgres. It drops to 0 during the restart. It stays 1 in the two pause variants, because the exporter goes straight to Postgres and does not use the proxy: only the API's path is cut. Stale-series caution: the last value can linger for a scrape interval.

spec.title: 503s by raw error code (server)
spec.description: ep_db_errors_by_code_total (ADDED BY B8, server). Expect 57P01 (admin_shutdown) / terminated / ECONNRESET at the start of a restart, ECONNREFUSED while it is down, 57P03 (cannot_connect_now) while Postgres starts up, pool_timeout when the pool has no free connection. The code tells which part of the outage is which. Surprising: only pool_timeout (the pool is exhausted by hung connections).

spec.title: Pool: total, idle, waiting, max
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_total / _idle / _waiting / _max. Healthy: total near max, idle > 0. In the outage the dead connections leave (total falls) or stay stuck (total stays at max with idle 0 and waiting growing). Surprising: total = max, idle = 0 and waiting > 0 after the database is back = the pool is clogged with connections that never answer.

spec.title: Pool connections opened / removed per second
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_connects_total, ep_pg_pool_removes_total, ep_pg_pool_idle_errors_total (ADDED BY B8, server). A clean reconnect = a burst of removes (dead connections thrown away) followed by a burst of connects. Surprising: no removes at all in pause_blackhole (nothing tells the pool the connections are dead).

spec.title: Postgres backends and commits
spec.description: Sessions in pg_stat_activity for the eventpulse database (postgres-exporter) and commits per second (pg_stat_database_xact_commit). Backends fall to about 0 in the restart and come back with the pool. In the pauses they stay: Postgres does not know the client is gone until TCP gives up. Commits per second should follow the 202 rate. Exporter caveat: during the restart the exporter itself has no data, so there are gaps.

spec.title: Pool wait and query time p99 (server)
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_wait_seconds (time waiting for a connection, capped by the 2 s pool timeout) and ep_pg_query_duration_seconds. Only requests that got a connection are observed in the query histogram, so a long outage leaves gaps instead of high values.

spec.title: CPU of the pinned groups (host, busy %)
spec.description: node_cpu_seconds_total (not idle) on the cores of each group: server, k6, postgres (variables cpu_server, cpu_k6, cpu_postgres). The server CPU may fall in the outage (requests fail fast, no queries) or rise (error handling). Postgres CPU spikes during the start and crash recovery.

spec.title: Server process CPU (user / system)
spec.description: process_cpu_user_seconds_total and process_cpu_system_seconds_total of the node process, in cores (1 = one core).

spec.title: Requests in flight and open client connections (server)
spec.description: http_requests_in_flight (Little's law: rate x time in the system) and http_connections_open. During a black hole the in-flight count climbs to about rate x timeout, because every request waits. Surprising: in flight stays high after the fault is over.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations (must be 0)
spec.description: k6_dropped_iterations_total rate. In B8 a pause can fill all VUs with waiting requests (rate x 10 s timeout = 20000 > 8000 maxVUs). Dropped iterations > 0 in a pause run mean the generator, not the server, stopped sending: those events were never offered, so the loss count must not use the offered rate. The k6 series are not marked stale after a run: the last value can linger.

spec.title: k6 VUs in use / max
spec.description: k6_vus and k6_vus_max. If vus reaches vus_max the generator ran out of users (see dropped iterations).

spec.title: k6 cores busy % (keep under 70)
spec.description: Host CPU on the k6 cores (cpu_k6). Keep under about 70 % so the generator is not the bottleneck. Thousands of waiting VUs in a pause cost memory more than CPU.

spec.title: Event loop lag p99 (server)
spec.description: nodejs_eventloop_lag_p99_seconds. A lag in the tens of ms means the Node process itself is struggling (not the database). Should stay small even in the outage.

spec.name: cpu_server
spec.label: CPUs: server (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the server group is pinned to (0,6), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_server"

spec.name: cpu_k6
spec.label: CPUs: k6 (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the k6 group is pinned to (3-4,9-10), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_k6"

spec.name: cpu_postgres
spec.label: CPUs: postgres (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the postgres group is pinned to (1-2,7-8), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_postgres"
